# CC18: 如园 Ru Yuan, "Ju Yuan, Garden of Likeness"

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC18` · Page: `/scenes/#CC18` · Row: `research/buildings/CC18-ru-yuan/`

## What it was

如园 Ru Yuan, "Garden of Likeness", in the south-east corner of Changchun Yuan, south-west of 鉴园 (S05 j83:18b; E0354). Finished in 1767 (E0358); early poems of 1768-70 call it 含芳书屋, the name 如园 appears from 1770 (E0356). Qianlong's poem of 1770 says its plan broadly follows the 瞻园 in the provincial treasury at 江宁 Nanjing, old garden of 徐达: 江寕藩司署中瞻園即明中山王徐逹西園之舊是園規制略倣之 (S05 j83:18b-19a; E0342); a covered way crossed the road over a double wall to 熙春园 on the south (E0342, E0356). 日下旧闻考: a three-bay gate facing west, 敦素堂, 冠霞阁 north-east of it and 明漪楼 further east; a hill path leads west to the east gate of 澹怀堂 (S05 j83:18b; E0354). Under Qianlong a piled hill split it into east and west courts, with 深宁堂 the main hall of the east court (S362). Jiaqing rebuilt it heavily, finished 1811, keeping the plan but adding winding galleries and pavilions and renaming every building except 新赏室: 深宁堂 became 延清堂; he chose ten views, the 如园十景, carved on stones beside them (S362; E0355, E0358). Daoguang and Xianfeng kept that layout, repairing rocks, shores and fittings (S362); Daoguang brought the dowager here for meals (E0356). Looted and burned in October 1860; the dig found 延清堂's floor bricks reddened and cracked through, and paths and hills reddened, from a long fire (S362; E0361).

From the inventory row: **built** poem 乾隆三十五年 1770 [j83:18b]; 1767; **changed** 1811 major repair, plaques changed; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S48, S01, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not in the Forty Scenes. After the rebuilding of 1811 Jiaqing chose the 如园十景, wrote a poem on each and had them carved on stones set beside the views (S362; E0358); the 2016-17 dig fixed the places of several (E0362). The ten names are in S361 (E0358), not listed on disk.

### How later sources differ

The 1811 rebuilding is the state of 1860 here, not the Qianlong garden (S362). S362 compares four plans: 如园地盘全样 (NLC, 圆明园卷续编 第八函 p.25), 长春园全图准底 (1814-1858), the 三园地盘河道全图 of about 1873 (Palace Museum) and the 1933 遗址形势图: Tongzhi may have made small repairs (the 挹霞亭 and 待月台 bases, the rockery west of 延清堂, the 镜香池 outlet) and removed a hexagonal pavilion north of the earth hill (S362). After 1911 rocks, stone and bricks were carried off; under the Japanese occupation farmers levelled hills and filled water for rice (S362).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

延清堂: the front bay of the first range without columns (减柱造) to give an open hall; the second range's side rooms closed by 碧纱橱, the west end room with a bed and hollow famille-rose tiles filled with sand on the floor; the third range cut into small closed rooms with beds (S362, from the Yangshi Lei interior plan). Under Jiaqing a 锦欢门幡 and a painted panel over a door are recorded (S362). Under Qianlong 深宁堂 had four flower paintings of the seasons and two trompe-l'oeil wall paintings 通景大画 (archive quoted in S362).

## What survives today

如园 was dug in two phases: 2012-13 for 芝兰室, 云萝山馆 and 听泉榭, and from November 2016 for 延清堂 and the hill paths; burning shows across the whole garden, and part is kept unexcavated (S330; E0363). From the dig and his own survey, 周秋彤 gives 延清堂 as a base 25.344 x 22.464 m and 1 m high, five bays of 4.16 and 3.84 m with a 1.664 m gallery round, three depth rows of 5.12, 6.4 and 5.12 m, a south terrace 19.68 x 7.968 m, a north terrace 12.3 x 9.3 m and a landing stage to the north (S362 sect. 三). Floors were 金砖 with a panel of hollow famille-rose tiles; roof tiles found are grey (S362).

Dug by 北京市文物研究所 in 2012 (west part; 芝兰室, 云萝山馆, 听泉榭) and 2016-2017 (second phase, with 延清堂) (S362; E0363). Site about 19,000 m2, buildings 2,800 m2, 3,800 m2 opened; 芝兰室, 云萝山馆, 听泉榭, 延清堂, 含碧楼, 挹霞亭, 观丰榭, 引胜轩, rockery, paths and shores found (E0363); over a thousand finds, among them a stone with a Jiaqing inscription, 金砖 floor bricks and famille-rose tiles, and several of the ten views placed (E0362). At 延清堂 27 of 50 column bases remain; the north terrace lies under the park's ring road and was not dug (S362).

## Modern reconstructions, not evidence (7)

Never a source for a size or a position here.

周秋彤's restoration study of 延清堂 (R0015; plan R0080, section R0081, elevation R0059, interior R0060) is built from the 2016-17 dig, three Yangshi Lei sheets (065-0002-02, 065-0004-01/-02) and the 奏销档, with roof pitches taken by analogy with 景福宫 and 景福阁 (S362): use its figures, not its drawings. The Central Academy of Fine Arts' digital 如园 (R0075, 2020; video R0074) states no method on disk.

## Gaps and wishlist

Only 延清堂 has a published measured reconstruction (S362, R0015, R0080, R0081, R0059). The other halls of the dig (芝兰室, 云萝山馆, 听泉榭, 含碧楼) have no published sizes on disk; the Yangshi Lei sheets 样065-0002/0004 (E0360) are cited, not seen. Names on S01 at CC18 (延清堂) are Jiaqing's, which is right for 1860.

CC18-02 敦素堂, CC18-03 冠霞阁, CC18-04 明漪楼 are Qianlong names (S05 j83:18b).** CC18-02 敦素堂, CC18-03 冠霞阁, CC18-04 明漪楼 are Qianlong names (S05 j83:18b); S362 says Jiaqing renamed every building in 1811 except 新赏室, so these names were gone by 1860.
